subject: E2E latency acceptance & measurement arrangement for ArborData
messages:
From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@arbordata.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: demo — latency/streaming targets + next steps

Laura / Ben / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the clarity on routing and fallback behavior. Per our internal SRE review I wanted to capture ArborData's acceptance criteria so we can get a scoped test plan in place. High-level goals:

- Production traffic profile: long-lived streaming sessions (average 18s of active streaming per session), ~50 concurrent sessions in peak, ~1.2M tokens/hour across the pool.
- E2E targets we need to validate (observed at our API gateway to user-facing response): p95 < 120 ms, p99 < 400 ms for short-turn (<= 128 tokens) interactive responses. For longer streaming (chunked responses) we expect stable append latency of < 80 ms per chunk and no buffering spikes.
- Throughput: sustain ~60 rps for short-turn API path and ~50 concurrent streaming sessions without tail spikes above 800 ms.

Attached is our last 24h extract from the incumbent vendor (vendor_latency_report.pdf) so you have a baseline. Two asks to move to a mutual action plan:

1) Can Redwood run a hosted-side trial (isolated test tenant / API key) with an agreed traffic replay so we can compare apples-to-apples to our incumbent?
2) What request-level instrumentation will Redwood provide? We need per-request trace IDs and per-chunk timing to map spikes back to your logs.

Procurement wise: if the trial validates the SLOs we can move quickly on a 6–12 month reserved capacity commit. Rohit (cc'd) will own the procurement cadence.

Next steps we propose from ArborData: we'll share a 3-minute traffic replay and a small corpus of representative payloads by EOD Monday. Please confirm the test windows you can run and any limits on concurrency you recommend for a first pass.

- Jamie

--
Jamie Park
Head of Product Operations | ArborData
jamie.park@arbordata.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@arbordata.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo — latency/streaming targets + next steps

Jamie — thanks for the clear summary and for the vendor extract. We can absolutely set up an isolated hosted trial and instrument everything you asked for. Quick confirmations and proposed schedule:

- Instrumentation: Redwood will emit per-request trace_id and token/chunk-level timing in the trial logs; we can provide a short CSV export format and a link to the trial logs in the Console.
- Test window: propose a 2-hour replay window during low production hours and a focused 30-minute high-concurrency streaming stress run. That should give us clear p95/p99 comparison points.
- Regions: we'll run the trial in us-east-1 (same as your gateway) unless you prefer otherwise.

I've attached our 1-page SLO measurement checklist (redwood_slo_checklist.pdf) — it outlines what we'll measure and the sample sizes we recommend for valid p99 estimates. Proposed next checkpoint: Ben and Aditya will suggest a technical runbook and required sample payloads by Monday morning; if that looks good we'll lock the slot for Wednesday UTC.

Thanks — looking forward to the replay.

- Laura

Laura Bennett
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jamie Park <jamie.park@arbordata.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo — latency/streaming targets + next steps

Jamie — quick technical clarifications from our side so we can size the trial correctly:

1) Concurrency definition: when you say ~50 concurrent sessions, do you mean 50 active open streaming connections (long-lived) or 50 simultaneous token-generation contexts? For the stress run we need to model both.
2) Short-turn path: confirm that your p95/p99 requirement (120/400 ms) is measured end-to-end from your gateway to final user event (i.e., includes TLS, LB, all downstream hops). That matches how we plan to report but want to be explicit.
3) Backpressure/timeout behavior: how does your client handle chunk drops? Any hard timeouts we should avoid during the trial?

Proposed acceptance envelope for an initial hosted run (this is conservative and compatible with your stated goals):
- Short-turn (<=128 tokens) target: p95 <= 180 ms, p99 <= 500 ms. If the hosted trial meets ArborData's stricter internal thresholds (120/400) we'll mark that as full pass.
- Streaming: per-chunk append latency median < 50 ms and 99th < 200 ms for the trial traffic; no more than 1% of chunks > 500 ms.

Operational asks from ArborData prior to the run: a replay capture (pcap-style or kinesis extract) and a small set of sample payloads (5–10). We'll also need a test API key and expected peak concurrency window.

If you can push the replay and payloads by today EOD we can provision the trial tenant and schedule the run for Wed 06/30 03:00–05:00 UTC.

- Ben

Ben Carter
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@arbordata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rohit Mehra <rohit.m@arbordata.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo — latency/streaming targets + next steps

Ben / Laura — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers:

- Concurrency: 50 concurrent sessions = 50 active streaming connections (clients keep a connection open while they stream). We will also include a burst profile for token-level concurrency in the replay.
- p95/p99 baseline: yes, our internal SLOs are measured from gateway edge to user-facing response; we will provide our measurement script so both sides compute percentiles the same way.
- Timeouts: client SDK enforces a 12s inactivity timeout and will attempt one retry per request if a chunk is lost; we'll flag any retry events in the replay.

We will upload the replay (3-minute sample) and 8 representative payloads to the HubSpot file link you shared by EOD today. Rohit will also send a short approval note to procurement if the trial meets the acceptance criteria.

Please confirm the API key format and any rate limits you place on trial tenants (especially burst concurrency caps). Also, please share the console link where we can stream logs during the run.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the run.

- Jamie

--
Jamie Park
Head of Product Operations | ArborData
